summary.goal:
Build a small library management system in this repository (Node.js, ES modules, no dependencies), with a command-line interface, persistence, validation, tests and documentation.

Storage: one JSON file, default `data/library.json` relative to the current directory; every command accepts `--data <path>` to use another file. Create the file on first use. Ids are integers assigned in order per entity type, starting at 1.

Modules (each with its own tests in test/ using node:test):
- src/books.js: addBook({ title, author, copies = 1 }), listBooks({ available } = {}); a book is { id, title, author, copies, available }.
- src/members.js: addMember({ name }); a member is { id, name }.
- src/loans.js: checkout({ bookId, memberId, days = 14, today }), returnLoan({ loanId, today }), listLoans({ memberId, overdue, today } = {}), report({ today }). A loan is { id, bookId, memberId, out, due, returned: null | date, fine }. Dates are strings YYYY-MM-DD; `today` defaults to the current date. Rules: checkout fails when the book has no available copy or the member already has 3 active loans; returning a loan after its due date charges a fine of 0.50 per day late, capped at 20.00; returning a loan twice fails.

CLI: bin/library.js, run as `node bin/library.js <command> [options] [--data <path>]`. Every successful command prints one JSON value on stdout and exits 0. Every failure prints `{ "error": "<message>" }` on stderr and exits 2 (unknown command or missing option: exit 1).
- `add-book --title <t> --author <a> [--copies <n>]` prints the book.
- `add-member --name <n>` prints the member.
- `checkout --book <id> --member <id> [--days <n>] [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints the loan.
- `return --loan <id> [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints the loan with its fine.
- `list-books [--available]` prints an array of books.
- `list-loans [--member <id>] [--overdue] [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints an array of loans (`--overdue` keeps only active loans whose due date is before today).
- `report [--today <YYYY-MM-DD>]` prints { books, copies, available, members, activeLoans, overdue, finesOwed } where finesOwed is the sum of the fines of every returned loan.

Add a "test" script to package.json so that `npm test` runs every test, and write a README.md that documents the modules, every command with an example, and the rules. npm test must pass.

report.summary:
Created the M1 CLI entry point `bin/library.js` and its test suite `test/cli-core.test.js`.

`bin/library.js` is an ESM executable (`#!/usr/bin/env node`, mode 755) that reads the command from `argv[0]`, parses the remaining arguments into a flag map, and dispatches through a `COMMANDS` table — the extension point milestone 2 will add `checkout`, `return`, `list-loans` and `report` to. The parser knows the value options listed in design §5.6 (`--title --author --copies --name --book --member --days --today --loan --data`) and the boolean flags `--available`/`--overdue`; `--copies` is converted with `Number(...)`, and an omitted (or `undefined`) `--data` falls through to `DEFAULT_DATA_PATH` via the storage default parameter, so no special casing is needed. Only `add-book`, `add-member` and `list-books` have handlers; the other four commands are still `unknown command` with exit 1.

Exit-code behaviour follows §7: success writes exactly one compact JSON value plus a newline to stdout and exits 0; a throw from a module writes `{"error":"<message>"}` plus a newline to stderr and exits 2; usage problems (missing command, unknown command, unknown option, unexpected positional argument, option without a value) write the same stderr shape and exit 1. An option is treated as valueless when it is the last argument or the next token starts with `--`, which turns `add-book --title --author X` into a clean usage error instead of a confusing one. The entry point sets `process.exitCode` rather than calling `process.exit()`, so stdout is always flushed before exit.

The 12 tests in `test/cli-core.test.js` spawn real processes with `spawnSync(process.execPath, [bin/library.js, ...args])` against `fs.mkdtempSync` temp `--data` files (never `data/library.json`, except one test that runs with `cwd` set to the temp dir and no `--data` to prove the default path). They cover success shapes, single-line stdout, empty stderr, persistence and id/nextId advance across separate invocations, the `--available` filter, the empty-catalog case creating the file, the untouched-file guarantee on rejection, six module-rejection cases at exit 2, and eleven usage cases at exit 1.

projectEvents.summary: Created the storage layer for the library system. src/storage.js exports exactly the design §5.1 surface: DEFAULT_DATA_PATH ("data/library.json"), emptyData(), loadData(dataPath), saveData(data, dataPath), updateData(dataPath, fn), nextId(data, kind), findById(list, id). All file I/O is synchronous node:fs. loadData creates an empty file (with parent directories) when the target is missing; saveData does mkdir -p and writes JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) plus a trailing newline; updateData loads, calls fn, saves, and returns fn's value, so a throw inside fn leaves the file untouched. nextId allocates per-kind ids from data.nextId starting at 1; findById returns the element or null. package.json gained only "scripts": { "test": "node --test" } (name, version, type unchanged, no dependencies added) and .gitignore gained data/. test/storage.test.js covers the missing-file/empty-data path, save/load round-trip, on-disk formatting, per-kind nextId counting across reloads, updateData persistence and return value, updateData leaving the file byte-identical when fn throws, and findById.

Created src/dates.js with the seven exports from design §5.2 (today, isDate, assertDate, parseDate, formatDate, addDays, daysBetween) and test/dates.test.js. All arithmetic runs on UTC midnight (Date.UTC / getUTC* / millisecond math), while today() derives the local calendar date before normalising to UTC. isDate validates both the strict YYYY-MM-DD pattern and real-calendar reality via a UTC round-trip, so 2026-2-3 and 2026-02-30 are rejected. assertDate throws Error('<label> must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD format') exactly as specified in §6. Tests cover the 2024 leap day, 2023-02-28, month/year rollover, negative differences, equal dates, and the invalid strings.

Created src/books.js implementing the design §5.3 surface (addBook, listBooks) and test/books.test.js covering the required cases. addBook validates and trims title/author, requires an integer copies >= 1 (defaulting to 1), stores { id, title, author, copies, available: copies } with the id from nextId(data, "book"), persists via updateData, and returns a plain copy. listBooks sorts by id ascending and filters to available > 0 when the available option is truthy. Both functions go through src/storage.js only (updateData/nextId); books.js has no direct file I/O and imports nothing else. Tests build their own temp data file with fs.mkdtempSync and never touch data/library.json.

Created src/members.js implementing addMember({ name, dataPath } = {}) per design §5.4: trims name, throws Error('name is required') for non-string/blank values, allocates an id with nextId(data, 'member'), persists { id, name } through updateData, and returns a copy of the stored member. Structure mirrors the existing src/books.js. Added test/members.test.js covering the id sequence, trimming, validation errors (missing/empty/whitespace/non-string/null), persistence across calls, and that member ids do not advance when books are added.

Created the M1 CLI entry point `bin/library.js` and its test suite `test/cli-core.test.js`.

`bin/library.js` is an ESM executable (`#!/usr/bin/env node`, mode 755) that reads the command from `argv[0]`, parses the remaining arguments into a flag map, and dispatches through a `COMMANDS` table — the extension point milestone 2 will add `checkout`, `return`, `list-loans` and `report` to. The parser knows the value options listed in design §5.6 (`--title --author --copies --name --book --member --days --today --loan --data`) and the boolean flags `--available`/`--overdue`; `--copies` is converted with `Number(...)`, and an omitted (or `undefined`) `--data` falls through to `DEFAULT_DATA_PATH` via the storage default parameter, so no special casing is needed. Only `add-book`, `add-member` and `list-books` have handlers; the other four commands are still `unknown command` with exit 1.

Exit-code behaviour follows §7: success writes exactly one compact JSON value plus a newline to stdout and exits 0; a throw from a module writes `{"error":"<message>"}` plus a newline to stderr and exits 2; usage problems (missing command, unknown command, unknown option, unexpected positional argument, option without a value) write the same stderr shape and exit 1. An option is treated as valueless when it is the last argument or the next token starts with `--`, which turns `add-book --title --author X` into a clean usage error instead of a confusing one. The entry point sets `process.exitCode` rather than calling `process.exit()`, so stdout is always flushed before exit.

The 12 tests in `test/cli-core.test.js` spawn real processes with `spawnSync(process.execPath, [bin/library.js, ...args])` against `fs.mkdtempSync` temp `--data` files (never `data/library.json`, except one test that runs with `cwd` set to the temp dir and no `--data` to prove the default path). They cover success shapes, single-line stdout, empty stderr, persistence and id/nextId advance across separate invocations, the `--available` filter, the empty-catalog case creating the file, the untouched-file guarantee on rejection, six module-rejection cases at exit 2, and eleven usage cases at exit 1.

projectEvents.summary:
Created src/loans.js with the four design §5.5 exports (checkout, returnLoan, listLoans, report) and test/loans.test.js with 19 cases; `node --test test/loans.test.js` passes and the full suite still passes (70 tests).

Implementation notes: all four functions read/mutate/write through storage.updateData, so a rejected operation leaves the data file byte-identical (the rules and lookups all run inside the updateData callback, and argument/date validation runs before it, so nothing is even created on a rejected call). checkout stores { id, bookId, memberId, out, due, returned: null, fine: 0 } with due = addDays(out, days), pushes the loan, decrements book.available, and returns a copy. returnLoan sets returned/fine, then increments book.available. Fines use daysBetween(due, returned), 0 when not late, otherwise min(0.5 * daysLate, 20) rounded to 2 decimals. listLoans sorts by id, then filters by memberId and, when overdue is truthy, to returned === null && due < reference date. report sums copies/available over books, counts members, counts active and overdue loans, and sums the fines of returned loans (rounded).

Decisions: the reference date is resolved once before updateData as `today === undefined ? dates.today() : dates.assertDate(today, "today")`, so a bad --today is rejected by every entry point with the §6 message without touching the file. Rule checks in checkout follow the §6 table order, which means availability is reported before the 3-loan limit. `listLoans` compares memberId strictly (undefined = no filter); the CLI already Number()-converts options. Fine arithmetic is rounded with Math.round(x * 100) / 100, and finesOwed is rounded after summing. returnLoan only increments available when the book is found, so a hand-edited file missing the book cannot turn into a TypeError.

One test-design consequence worth knowing: because availability is checked before the 3-active-loan limit, the limit test uses a deliberately over-copied book (4 copies) so the fourth checkout reaches the member-limit error rather than "no available copy".
